theorem.statement:
For each \(N\) and allowed observed design, let \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) be the exact attained critical value over \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), and let
\[
C_N^{\mathrm{att}}=\{b\in\mathcal B:T_N(b)\le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}.
\]
The Gaussian reference quantile is uniformly continuous on the bounded-amplitude, tangent-plane, and endpoint-half-plane compactification, and
\[
\inf_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
\Pr\!\left\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
\le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\right\}=1-\alpha.                           \tag{29}
\]
For the actual observed-law experiment,
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
P_N\{\beta\in C_N^{\mathrm{att}}\}=1-\alpha,                               \tag{30}
\]
and there is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on the fixed model and level constants, such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(C_N^{\mathrm{att}})\le C N^{-1/2}\quad P_N\text{-almost surely}                              \tag{31}
\]
uniformly over the model class.  The conclusions include zero amplitude, bounded and diverging local amplitudes, exponent endpoints, the one-dimensional logarithmic elbow window, and nonconvergent allowed-design sequences.  Equation (30) is an asymptotic observed-law statement; at fixed \(N\), (29) is exact only for the Gaussian reference statistic.  The critical value is mathematically defined and attained, but no terminating certified numerical approximation to it is asserted.
theorem.justification: The exact attained Gaussian critical value yields asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\), while moment separation gives a deterministic root-\(N\) diameter bound.
theorem.gap: The theorem separates exact mathematical calibration from computation: a terminating certified numerical approximation of the continuum maximum remains open, and no finite-sample observed-law equality is claimed.
theorem.consumer: Conditional on the stated Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics, the result supplies the exact least-favorable asymptotic profile calibration for the homogeneous county-centroid slope analysis.

added_lemmas.statement:
For each fixed \(N\) and allowed observed design, \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\) is compact.  The law of
\[
d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
\]
is atomless and has a strictly increasing distribution function on \((0,\infty)\); its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is continuous in \((\lambda,p)\).  Hence the maximum defining \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is attained and
\[
 \inf_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
 \Pr\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
       \le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}=1-\alpha.                           \tag{20}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 0<c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha},                       \tag{21}
\]
and both bounds are uniform over the allowed designs after compactification.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(N\) and an allowed design.  Let \(\Theta_N\) be the subset of
\[
[-A_{\max},A_{\max}]\times[p_{\min},p_{\max}]
   \times\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nuis}}
\]
on which the determinant-margin inequality holds at every \(\omega\in\mathbb R^d\).  The displayed product is compact by the amplitude, exponent, and nuisance-compactness assumptions.  For each fixed \(\omega\), the determinant-margin inequality is a closed condition in the coordinates of this product, because the three spectra are continuous functions of those coordinates.  Hence \(\Theta_N\), an intersection of closed subsets of a compact set, is compact.  The ideal stencil contains finitely many fixed distances, so its power-law moment is a finite linear combination of functions \(r^{2p}\).  Thus \(P_\star(p)\), and hence \(K_d(p)\), is continuous on the exponent interval; positivity is part of their definitions.  Since \(h_N,c_X,c_W>0\), the map
\[
(A,p,c_X,c_W,\alpha_X,\alpha_W,\alpha_C)
 \longmapsto
 \left(\frac{A K_d(p)\sqrt N h_N^{2p-1}}{\sqrt{c_Xc_W}},p\right)             \tag{22}
\]
is continuous.  By the definition of the physically attainable set, its image is \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\).  An allowed model supplies at least one legal tuple, so this image is nonempty.  It is therefore compact.

Set
\[
S_{N,\lambda,p}=d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2.
\]
Write \(F_{N,\lambda,p}\) for the distribution function of \(S_{N,\lambda,p}\).  The profile-geometry compactification lemma gives
\[
F_{N,\lambda,p}(0)=0,
\qquad F_{N,\lambda,p}\text{ is continuous on }[0,\infty),
\qquad F_{N,\lambda,p}\text{ is strictly increasing on }(0,\infty).         \tag{23}
\]
In particular the quantile
\[
k_N(\lambda,p)=\inf\{x\ge0:F_{N,\lambda,p}(x)\ge1-\alpha\}                 \tag{24}
\]
is positive, unique, and satisfies
\[
F_{N,\lambda,p}\{k_N(\lambda,p)\}=1-\alpha.                                \tag{25}
\]
If \((\lambda_r,p_r)\to(\lambda,p)\), use the same Gaussian vector \(G_N\) for all indices.  Continuity of \(q_N\) and the fact that distance to a fixed closed set is continuous give
\[
S_{N,\lambda_r,p_r}\longrightarrow S_{N,\lambda,p}
\quad\text{almost surely}.                                                    \tag{26}
\]
Equation (23) and (26) imply pointwise convergence of the corresponding distribution functions.  If the quantiles in (24) failed to converge to \(k_N(\lambda,p)\), a subsequence would lie on one side of a fixed intermediate point.  Evaluating the distribution functions at that point and using (23) would contradict (24)--(25).  Thus \(k_N\) is continuous.  Compactness of \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\) now supplies a maximizer \((\lambda_*,p_*)\), and
\[
c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}=k_N(\lambda_*,p_*).                              \tag{27}
\]
For every \((\lambda,p)\) in the physical set, (25) and (27) give
\[
F_{N,\lambda,p}(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}})\ge1-\alpha,
\]
while equality holds at \((\lambda_*,p_*)\).  This proves (20).

For the upper bound, the cone contains the line \(\{a q_N(p):a\in\mathbb R\}\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{N,\lambda,p}
&\le \inf_{a\in\mathbb R}
 \|G_N+\lambda q_N(p)-a q_N(p)\|_{H_N}^2\\
&=\inf_{b\in\mathbb R}\|G_N-bq_N(p)\|_{H_N}^2,                              \tag{28}
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\|x\|_{H_N}^2=x^{\mathsf T}H_N^{-1}x\).  After whitening, the last quantity is the squared norm of the projection of a standard three-dimensional Gaussian vector onto the two-dimensional orthocomplement of \(H_N^{-1/2}q_N(p)\).  It has the \(\chi^2_2\) law.  Equations (24) and (28) prove the upper inequality in (21).

Finally, the profile-geometry lemma extends the quantile map continuously to a sequentially compact family containing all bounded-amplitude, tangent-plane, and endpoint-half-plane limits, including limits of nonconvergent designs.  At every point of that compactification the limiting squared distance has probability zero at zero by the same lemma.  Since \(1-\alpha>0\), its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is strictly positive.  A continuous positive function on a compact set has a positive minimum; call it \(c_0\).  This proves the lower inequality in (21) and the asserted uniform continuity.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each \(N\) and observed design, form the physically attainable set \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), define
\[
c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}
=\max_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
\inf\!\left\{x\ge0:
\Pr\!\left[d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\le x\right]
\ge1-\alpha\right\},
\]
and set
\[
C_N^{\mathrm{att}}=\{b\in\mathcal B:T_N(b)\le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}.
\]
The handle uses the bounded-amplitude, tangent-plane, and endpoint-half-plane compactification to justify attainment and uniform transfer to the actual experiment.  It defines an exact mathematical critical value; a terminating certified numerical approximation is not part of the construction.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen construction incorrectly included certified interval arithmetic. The proved result uses the exact attained critical value and leaves certified numerical approximation as a separate open question.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, to the continuum maximum defining \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) on every allowed actual design.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions give abstract compactness and uniform continuity but no effective two-sided representation of the determinant-constrained physical set, no certified feasible inner witnesses, and no computable convergence modulus for the Gaussian quantile optimization.
open_obligations.attempted: Outward interval enclosures can provide conservative upper values, but without certified inner feasibility and a quantitative modulus they do not certify the exact maximum or a prescribed approximation error; therefore no terminating rate such as \(N^{-1}\) is claimed.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact maximum \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is attained, its reference quantile map is uniformly continuous on the proved compactification, and
\[
0<c_0\le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}
\]
uniformly.  For each fixed input pair \((\lambda,p)\), the defining three-dimensional Gaussian probability is explicit.  These facts establish mathematical existence and a conservative analytic upper bound, but not a terminating certified approximation of the continuum maximum.

prose_updates.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes generate a finite-dimensional mean cone \(\beta\mathbf 1+B_Nq_N(p)\) whose secants and tangents remain uniformly separated from the slope direction. The actual quasi-uniform-design Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization yield conservative uniform inference, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching lower bounds through every vanishing signed cross-tail. In addition, the exact least-favorable Gaussian critical value over the physically attainable amplitude--exponent set is attained and gives asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\), with a pathwise \(O(N^{-1/2})\) diameter through zero, local, divergent, endpoint, elbow, and nonconvergent-design regimes. This equality is not a finite-sample observed-law claim, and a terminating certified numerical approximation of the exact critical value remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results deliver Gaussian inference for scalar covariance combinations. They do not provide actual-design, design-uniform slope inference or exact least-favorable asymptotic profile calibration when the observation-scale signed cross-tail is local to zero and its exponent is unidentified.
project_justification.niche: The exact Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget model isolates a nonregular finite-dimensional nuisance cone in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly. Exact affine filters control arbitrary quasi-uniform designs in dimensions one and two, while the physical amplitude set distinguishes bounded, divergent, endpoint, and elbow regimes.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, conservative uniform coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, matching honest lower bounds, and an exact attained Gaussian critical value whose profile set has asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\). Certified numerical evaluation of the continuum critical-value maximum is retained as a separate open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate the problem by showing that decay of high-frequency exposure--confounder coherence can identify a spatial slope; their spectral construction informs the observation-scale tail parameter used here. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broad Gaussian-field classes; their result informs the local-filter architecture, while the present inference theorem is for the narrower no-nugget signed-cross-tail class. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott obtain root-\(N\) Gaussian covariance estimation from preconditioned quadratic forms on irregular lattices, and Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs; both inform the finite-matrix proof. Lim and Stein prove normality of filtered cross-periodograms on lattices and inform the cross-form covariance analysis. Zhang studies scalar Mat\'ern microergodic equivalence, while Li studies Bayesian posterior and Bernstein--von Mises behavior for Mat\'ern covariance parameters. Andrews and Mikusheva inform weak-identification calibration but do not analyze this spatial curved cone or its tangent and endpoint limits. Burman, Ogburn and Datta provide the conditional county-centroid PM2.5 and COVID-19 consumer and a distinct plurality-based identifying model. The exact critical value proved here is an attained mathematical Gaussian quantile; no cited work or present argument supplies its terminating certified continuum computation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model is restricted to deterministic quasi-uniform designs in dimensions one and two, no nugget, known marginal smoothness one-half, stationary Gaussian fields, compact scale and range nuisance, and the stated signed parametric cross-tail. The exact-attainable profile set has asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\) and pathwise root-\(N\) diameter; only its Gaussian reference calibration is exact at fixed \(N\). A terminating certified numerical approximation of the exact continuum critical value is not proved, so the conservative chi-square critical value remains the directly specified fallback. The scope excludes unknown marginal-smoothness adaptation, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and broader covariance classes. The county-centroid PM2.5 and COVID-19 use is conditional on empirical Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics and does not itself establish a nonparametric causal estimand.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem turns the abstract physical Gaussian maximum into an exact asymptotic observed-law calibration and preserves the root-\(N\) diameter uniformly through all attainable regimes.
statement_notes.gap: Exact attainment and asymptotic coverage do not by themselves yield a terminating certified numerical approximation; that effective-computation problem remains open, and finite-sample observed-law equality is not claimed.
statement_notes.consumer: When the Mat\'ern and design diagnostics hold, the theorem supplies the exact least-favorable asymptotic profile calibration for the homogeneous county-centroid slope analysis of Burman, Ogburn and Datta.
